input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine your eyes are like two little toy balloons on strings.

When you want to cross your eyes, you can pull the strings together and make the balloons bump into each other. That’s easy because your eyes can move that way.

But if you try to pull the strings in the opposite direction—like, way far apart—your arms (or the strings) will get tired and you can’t make the balloons go past a certain point. That’s because your eyes are only made to move so much before they bump into your face or it feels weird.

So, you can cross your eyes easily, but you can’t pull them apart super far because your body is built that way to keep your eyes safe!
